rationale:
ROUND 2. Round 1 (f0591cb2) came back REVISE on a gating objection from editquality: the --color-cta-bg-ink entry was grounded on `cta_text`, and the seat said that is not the surface the ink actually sits on. The seat was RIGHT, and chasing it found a defect the round-1 plan had not measured, so this round is a real change rather than a defence.

WHAT THE OBJECTION FOUND. The two consumers of that ink do not paint the button the same way [MEASURED 2026-08-25, content_components.html_template]: `call-to-action` paints `var(--color-cta-text, var(--color-primary-text))` and `tool-cta` hard-codes `var(--color-white, #fff)`. Same UI object, two faces, one of them underivable from the palette -- the bugs_open/113 layout-literal shape.

GROUNDING ON BOTH FACES WAS THE OBVIOUS FIX AND IT IS WRONG, not merely expensive. **7 live themes** pair a LIGHT band with a NEAR-BLACK ink (cta_bg #e9e2d3 / cta_text #1a1a1a: noted, idea, lendzy, loanzy, mortgagecalculator, remortgagecalculator, webdesign.co.uk) [MEASURED 2026-08-25]. There the two faces are #ffffff and #1a1a1a and NO single colour clears 4.5 on both; legibleInkFor falls through to its terminal branch and emits black at a worst ratio of ~1.2 -- a second invisible button, in the opposite direction from the one being repaired. So migration 630 CONVERGES the face instead, and the ink is then grounded on the one real surface.

SECOND CHANGE, found at the artefact rather than by review, and the reviewers' own precedent search surfaced the same objection upheld on 2026-08-06: **619 shipped nothing on its own.** Nothing files `template_changed` re-renders for a template edited by SQL (that fan-out is keyed to component-template-fixer's own component_id), so every page keeps serving its stored rendered_html with a green status. Measured: after 619 applied, a page-rerender dispatch reported COMPLETED for three finetuning.uk pages and all three still served the broken declaration, `page_components.updated_at` still reading 08-17/08-23/08-24. Migration 631 is the fan-out, scoped to the 9 pages that are actually broken rather than the 55 that are merely stale.

CENSUS CORRECTED. Round 1's verify block pinned `color-mix` uses at 1 using a needle too narrow to have proven it. Re-run position-classified over ALL 13 components that reference --color-cta-bg [MEASURED 2026-08-25, post-619]: as-a-color-value 0, in-a-gradient-stop 0, in-color-mix 1 (tool-password-entropy_pre_037, 0 live uses, pinned), as-a-background 13 (the legal use). The conclusion held; the evidence for it did not, and that is the second time a census here encoded its own answer.

plan.summary: Ground --color-cta-bg-ink on the button's REAL face (and converge that face so there is one), plus the template_changed fan-out without which migration 619 ships nothing.

edits.rationale: ROUND 2: grounded on the button's real face, and only after 630 made there be one. The entry is emitted only when a face is resolvable; with none, legibleInkFor's terminal branch compares two unmeasurable candidates, `0 >= 0` holds, and it hands back WHITE -- the exact 1.00:1 defect being repaired, confirmed by mutation M1 which emitted #ffffff. The comment now names both consumers' painted surfaces and records why grounding on both faces is wrong, so the next editor meets the 7-theme measurement rather than rediscovering it.

cta_bg is the one slot that may be a gradient, so every consumer needing a <color> comes through solidCTAFill; a caller reading palette["cta_bg"] directly is the defect. firstGradientStop is deliberately narrow -- hex stops only, which is what all 10 gradient themes actually hold (MEASURED 2026-08-25). Returning "" for rgb()/hsl()/named stops is the safe direction: the companion is then not emitted, every consumer falls through its own var() fallback, and behaviour is exactly today's. Widening it must bring its own contrast measurement.

ROUND 2 tests. The two-face test is replaced by the case that actually discriminates: a LIGHT band with a NEAR-BLACK ink (cta_bg #e9e2d3 / cta_text #1a1a1a, seven live themes), where the ink must be LIGHT. Mutation M4 -- ground on #ffffff instead of the face -- emits #816d41 scoring 3.48 on that face and the test goes RED. The earlier #F0F2F7 case was NOT discriminating (it is within a hair of white) and was dropped rather than kept as decoration. M1 (drop the face guard) and M2 (make legibleInkFor always keep its source) re-run and still fail their named tests.

edits.rationale: Heroes: DELETE the second `background:` declaration. The valid single declaration is already on the line above and covers both a gradient and a colour; the deleted line was cosmetic (an 82% color-mix toward the ink). The sibling heroes `hero`, `use-cases-hero` and `case-studies-hero` carry the SAME idiom against --color-primary, which is always a colour -- they are correct and are deliberately untouched, and they are the in-repo control for this diagnosis. Buttons: repoint the ink at var(--color-cta-bg-ink, var(--color-cta-bg)) -- the mandatory two-level form of the ink contract (inkPolicy.enabled's comment records 46 consumer rows, 0 bare), so this half is a NO-OP until the chassis roll emits the token and degrades to today's behaviour if the ink kill-switch is thrown. Needles were extracted from the live rows, not retyped; each matches exactly once.
edits.sketch:
UPDATE content_components SET html_template = replace(html_template,
  E'\n    background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--color-cta-bg, var(--color-primary)) 0%, color-mix(...) 100%);', '')
 WHERE name IN ('about-hero','contact-hero','services-hero') AND html_template LIKE '%...%';
-- + 2 button UPDATEs, + a DO/RAISE verify block

edits.rationale: A DO/RAISE, not a block of SELECTs: ON_ERROR_STOP does not treat a non-empty result as an error, so a SELECT-only verify cannot stop the COMMIT. INDUCED against pre-migration state -- the colour-stop arm RAISEd, and that is how a FOURTH row was found at all: my by-name census had encoded its own answer. Arms 2 and 4 read 2 and 0 pre-migration (both would raise); arm 3 reads 3 before and after and is stated as a post-condition against OVER-deletion rather than something that can fire early. The color-mix arm is PINNED at exactly 1 rather than cleared: tool-password-entropy_pre_037 has the same invalid-value fault but its harm is a missing panel tint, not unreadable text, and it has ZERO page_components uses -- repairing it needs a solid FILL companion, a different token from this legible INK, with no live consumer, which is the accumulating-opt-in-surface shape RFC_022 discourages. It is recorded as a known remainder in bugs_open/398, and the pin means a NEW component taking the same wrong turn refuses the migration rather than passing unnoticed.

IF n_mix <> 1 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '619: % use --color-cta-bg inside color-mix(), want exactly the 1 known unshipped row', n_mix; END IF;

edits.rationale: Restores the exact prior bytes, and says plainly in its header that doing so restores the DEFECT. Guarded so it cannot double-apply (the hero arm requires the gradient-stop line to be absent).

Converge tool-cta's button face on the palette slot its sibling already reads, so the CTA button has ONE face and an ink can be derived for it. Effect before the chassis roll: none on the 10 gradient themes (cta_text IS #ffffff there); on the 7 light-band themes the face becomes #1a1a1a and the ink falls through to cta_bg #e9e2d3, i.e. cream on near-black at ~12:1, an improvement on today's cream-on-white. Needle anchored on the ink line 619 wrote, so it cannot apply out of order; verified unique (1 occurrence of the anchored pair, 1 of the literal in the whole template).

  E'background: var(--color-white, #fff);\n    color: var(--color-cta-bg-ink',

plan.risks:
The button half is INERT until the next chassis roll -- var(--color-cta-bg-ink, var(--color-cta-bg)) resolves to the gradient until the renderer emits the companion, i.e. exactly today's behaviour. Deliberate: the alternative fallbacks were measured and all fail. --color-primary is illegible on a white button on 4 of 12 themes (theme-loanandmortgagecalculator-co-uk scores 1.24:1, trading one invisible button for another), and the raw first stop fails on 6 of 10. There is no correct token until this one exists.

The hero half is live on the next re-render of any page using those three components, across every site, not just finetuning.uk. On a solid-cta_bg site the visible change is losing a subtle 82% gradient sheen on the band; the fill colour is unchanged because the surviving declaration is the same token.

Re-render required: content_components is the template, the served pages hold rendered output. A page_rerender re-assembles from content_data plus the template, so the CSS updates and the copy is not regenerated -- which is what makes this compatible with the finetuning lane's standing copy hold.

firstGradientStop is narrow by construction and silently emits nothing for an rgb()/hsl()/named-colour stop. Today that set is empty; if a future palette uses one, the affected consumers revert to present-day behaviour rather than breaking, but the repair will not reach them and nothing will say so.

tool-password-entropy_pre_037 keeps three invalid color-mix() backgrounds. Unshipped (0 page_components uses) and a different harm class; pinned by the verify block and recorded in bugs_open/398 rather than fixed silently.

ROUND 2 — 630 changes tool-cta's button face on 60 live instances. On the 10 gradient themes it is a byte-level no-op in effect (cta_text IS #ffffff). On the 7 light-band themes the face flips white -> near-black; the ink then falls through to cta_bg (cream), which measures ~12:1, but this is a VISIBLE change to those sites and they are other lanes'. Not fanned out here: those pages re-render on their own schedule, and the one deliberate fan-out for CTA buttons comes after the chassis roll.

ROUND 2 — 631 files 9 rerenders across 3 sites, 2 of them other lanes' (gaswholesalers.com, robot-hands.com). Included because the defect is live there and the repair regenerates no copy. Owner ruling 2026-07-29 §3 requires TELLING them; a CONTRIB in each lane's directory is owed and is not discharged by the migration comment.

ROUND 2 — the 46 stale-but-not-broken pages are deliberately left. They serve a valid gradient sheen today and will converge to the flat band on their next natural re-render, at a moment nobody is watching. That is a knowingly deferred cosmetic drift, not an oversight.
